instructional_purpose: Establishes that a full finite clause can fill a slot that a single noun would otherwise fill, and that the slot confers a case value on the clause even though no case exponent is visible. linguistic_propositions.proposition: A clause filling a slot is assigned that slot's case value positionally, with no exponent appearing anywhere on the clause.

The comment slot after an emphatic abrogator carries nominative value while the comment slot after a copular abrogator carries accusative value, even though the embedded clause is surface-identical in both.
Cognition verbs admit a clause in their accusative-valued complement slot, alternating with a two-accusative construction that has no complementiser.
A clausal attribute inherits whatever case value its head noun carries.
A clause following a time-adverbial head occupies a genitive-valued second-construct slot.
The inventory of slot-bearing clause types contains exactly seven members.
A clause introduced by a relative pronoun after a definite head is an attributive clause bearing that head's case value.
A clause in the apodosis of a jussive conditional bears a slot, which this inventory omits entirely.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A grammatically complete clause bears no case value unless some governor assigns it a slot.
The complement of a relative pronoun bears no slot, although the relative construction as a whole may bear one.
An apodosis introduced by the connective particle bears a jussive-valued slot, while the same apodosis without it bears no slot.
The connective-particle rule as stated applies to conditional apodoses generally, without distinguishing jussive-governing from non-jussive-governing conditional particles.
A clause after an explanatory particle merely restates and therefore bears no slot.
An inserted parenthetical — prayer, oath, or gloss — bears no slot because it interrupts rather than fills a structure.
The response clause of an oath bears no slot.
A clause resuming discourse after a pause or topic shift bears no slot.
The inventory of non-slot-bearing clause types contains exactly seven members.
The opening-clause label is reserved for the first clause of a stretch of discourse; the identical string later in the same discourse is resumptive instead.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The state descriptor is accusative when a single word and accusative-valued when a clause.
A nominal state clause requires the state-waw.
A verbal state clause built on an imperfect verb may omit the waw, and when it does its subject must be the state-holder.
A nominal state clause must contain a pronoun coreferent with the state-holder.
The state-holder must be definite.
The state-holder may be either the subject or the object of the governing verb.
A prepositional or adverbial phrase functioning as a state descriptor itself occupies an accusative-valued slot.
A finite past-tense clause coordinated after a motion verb is a state clause.
A locative phrase after a posture verb is a state descriptor rather than an adverbial complement of that verb.
The state role is temporary and the attributive role permanent.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A nominal following the accompaniment connective is accusative and denotes concomitant circumstance rather than a second participant.
The construction requires a preceding verb or verbal equivalent.
When the second nominal can perform the event, the reading is coordination and its case matches the first nominal.
Whether the second nominal can perform the event determines the syntactic analysis.
The accusative exponent varies with noun class: fatha for singular and broken plural, ya for dual and sound masculine plural, kasra standing in for fatha with the sound feminine plural.
Where both readings are available the speaker selects by emphasis, coordination foregrounding joint action and accompaniment foregrounding a single main actor.
In the parse the accompaniment connective is a coordinating letter carrying an accompaniment sense.
Animate nominals may serve as accompaniment objects when the speaker foregrounds one actor.

instructional_purpose: Moves the syntactic focus from the sentence to the paragraph, teaching a set of connectors that manage topic, time, cause, place, contrast, and concession, and showing how they structure enumerated legal and scholarly prose.
concepts_taught: textual cohesion as a level of structure above the sentence

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The topic-shift particle requires the response particle before the comment; the comment cannot follow directly.
The nominal after the topic-shift particle is nominative as a topic on the usual analysis, while some grammarians assign accusative in certain constructions.
إذ refers to realised past time while إذا refers to future or hypothetical time.
حيث takes both a locative and a causal reading, resolved by context.
حيث is indeclinable on the damma and is followed by a full clause.
بينما is followed by a verbal clause, or by a nominal clause opening with a copular verb.
لمّا differs from إذ in presenting the first event as triggering the second.
The choice among connectors is determined by which relation is intended: enumeration, past cause, place or ground, simultaneity, trigger, consequence, or concession.
بينما is composed of the preposition-like element plus an attached particle.

instructional_purpose: Teaches the two-element numerals from eleven through nineteen: how the two elements are shaped relative to the gender of the counted noun, and how the counted noun itself is cased and numbered as a specifier.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The numerals eleven through nineteen consist of a unit element and a ten element joined directly, with no connective between them.
In thirteen through nineteen the unit element carries the gender marking opposite to that of the counted noun, while the ten element carries the marking agreeing with it.
In eleven and twelve both elements agree in gender with the counted noun.
The counted noun after these compounds is singular and accusative, functioning as a specifier.
The entire compound is indeclinable on fatha.
The twelve compound appears with its first element in the construct dual shape rather than the free dual shape.

select the shape of the ten element to agree with that gender

for eleven and twelve, select both element shapes to agree with that gender

the agreement rule applies to both elements only in the eleven and twelve compounds
the specifier must be singular, never plural
exceptions: eleven and twelve break the polarity pattern that governs the rest of the range

instructional_purpose: Covers the decade numerals and their compounds from twenty to ninety-nine, establishing that the decades are invariant for gender, inflect like a sound masculine plural, and take the same singular accusative specifier as the previous range.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The decade numerals do not change form according to the gender of the counted noun.
The decades inflect for case like the sound masculine plural, with one ending for the nominative and another shared by accusative and genitive.
Compound numerals from twenty-one to ninety-nine place the unit before the decade, joined by the connective.
Within a compound only the unit element varies for gender: units one and two agree with the counted noun, units three to nine take the opposite marking.
The counted noun after twenty through ninety-nine is singular and accusative as a specifier, identically to the previous range.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: After hundreds and thousands the counted noun is singular and genitive, in contrast to the singular accusative specifier of the eleven-to-ninety-nine ranges.
The hundred word is feminine, so units three to nine before it take the shape used with masculine counted nouns.
The thousand word is masculine, so units three to ten before it take the shape used with feminine counted nouns, and govern its broken plural.
The dual hundred and dual thousand lose their dual ending before the counted noun.
Ordinals one through ten follow the agent-participle template, with a suppletive irregular form for the first.
Ordinals follow the noun they qualify and agree with it in gender, case, and definiteness.
The second ordinal is a defective noun whose final glide is absent in the indefinite nominative and genitive.
In a multi-order numeral the counted noun appears once, at the end of the whole phrase, in the singular genitive.

instructional_purpose: Separates the two grammatical functions of a single quantifier word — asking for a quantity and exclaiming at one — and establishes the case of its specifier as the formal signal that distinguishes them, with discourse cues as a fallback where case is unrealised.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The interrogative use takes a singular accusative specifier.
The exclamatory use takes a genitive specifier which may be singular or plural.
The case of the specifier is the decisive formal signal separating the two uses.
Where case is unrealised, the distinction is drawn from whether an answer is expected, from emotional register, and from punctuation.
The exclamatory use expresses multitude together with wonder, sorrow, or pride, and is characteristic of classical verse.
Punctuation is a usable cue for the distinction.

misleading_shortcuts: the case-based mnemonic breaks where a preposition precedes the quantifier, a configuration the lesson omits
punctuation is treated as evidence although classical texts carry none and the cited verse has no punctuation
one cited verse contains a diptote specifier whose surface fatha would be misclassified by the case rule as literally stated
reading 'no answer expected' as 'no information conveyed', when the exclamatory use asserts multitude

name the function that case selects

state the reading
paradigms: a two-row function comparison table with answer expectation
a five-feature discriminator table covering meaning, answer expectation, specifier number, specifier case, and an illustration
separate example tables for each use with per-example specifier analysis
a four-row error-and-correction table

accusative and genitive exponents including tanwin

further specifier constructions
sarf_relevance: low — only the case exponents and the plural forms available to the specifier touch morphology
nahw_relevance: high — a single token whose function determines the case of the following word, with a stated but incomplete decision procedure
tutor_drill_relevance: high — the discriminator is objective wherever case is realised, and the error table gives four calibrated failure modes; drills must avoid the prepositional configuration the lesson omits
rich_hover_relevance: high — this is a textbook multifunction token: a hover that reports one sense will mis-gloss the other, and the correct sense is read off the following word rather than the token itself
corpus_pvn_relevance: particle entries (p) for the quantifier with two distinct senses keyed on the case it assigns; noun entries (n) only for specifier forms in their singular accusative and singular or plural genitive shapes
required_evidence: per occurrence: the realised case of the immediately following noun, whether a preposition precedes the quantifier, whether the specifier is diptote, and whether the surrounding discourse supplies an answer; an unvocalised occurrence with no reply in context is not resolvable and must be left open
uncertainty_flags: the case rule is presented as decisive without the exception created by a preceding preposition
one cited verse's specifier is a diptote whose genitive surfaces with a fatha exponent, which the stated rule would misread
punctuation is offered as a cue although the classical material adduced carries none
the relative preference between singular and plural specifiers after the exclamatory use is not attributed and varies between treatments
